body:
maria: Quick follow-up from the streaming retry thread. Proposal: shift primary responsibility for ephemeral resume/continue semantics to edge proxies. Gateway will carry opaque tokens and minimal routing info only. Rationale: faster resume path, fewer cross-gateway hops for validation. Tradeoffs: edge statefulness, memory pressure, and charging/accounting questions. Feedback?
aj: Clarify: are we moving token issuance + validation + short-lived lease into the edge? How does this behave when requests route through multiple frontdoors?
maria: Exactly. Edge mints a signed continuation token and keeps a small lease record. Gateways forward tokens verbatim. For multi-frontdoor we embed a route_sig that binds token to an allowed route set; route_sig prevents accidental cross-route resume unless allowed by policy.
devon: My main worry is state loss on edge crash. Two options: ephemeral-only (best-effort resume when same edge still alive) or replicate lightweight checkpoints to a durable store so another edge can honor resume. Durable replication adds IO/coordination.
andre: Durable checkpoints also change billing semantics. If edge is replaying tokens to upstream models, who gets billed for those tokens? Edge owner or the downstream model consumer? We need an explicit billing attribution model before shipping.
sre-oncall: Observability requirement: resumed sessions must be linkable to original request traces. Need resume_reason tag (e.g., EDGE_REBIND, CLIENT_RECONNECT, GATEWAY_RETRY) and resume_attempt counter. Also consider alerting when resume_success_rate drops.
maria: Operational compromise: keep leases in-memory for hot sessions and write a compact checkpoint blob to a durable store every few seconds for sessions marked "replicable". The checkpoint contains only session_id, route_hash, last_emitted_index, and a small KV_digest referencing a larger offload store (not full KV).
aj: Rehydrating KV from blob will be expensive for large contexts. We should design for partial replays: client replays the last R tokens (e.g., 128) upon reconnect to rebuild KV lazily. Upstream must accept bounded replay semantics.
devon: Partial-replay is pragmatic. It avoids heavy IO and makes resume probabilistic. Clients should see a short playback of recent tokens then continue. Document the client contract: on resume, client re-sends last N tokens, then normal streaming continues.
maria: Draft API contract snippet: 
```yaml
continue_token_v1: base64(signed{sid, route_hash, exp, flags})
resume_window_s: 45
replicate_interval_s: 5
partial_replay_tokens: 128
allow_rebind: true
```
andre: Security: key rotation for signing tokens is mandatory. Keep previous keys in a validation window at least equal to resume_window to avoid invalidation of in-flight tokens. Also scope tokens by tenant and role.
sre-oncall: Telemetry hooks: resume_latency_ms histogram, resume_failure_reason tag, and link to original trace_id via trace_parent or trace_link. Also ensure traces record whether resume used in-memory lease vs. durable rebind.
devon: Memory management: per-tenant soft caps and LRU eviction. When we evict a lease, we should return an explicit resume_unavailable message to client so they can do a full cold reconnect. Do not silently drop ability to resume.
aj: Need perf targets: median resume latency under 40ms for in-memory, under 200ms for rebind-with-checkpoint. I can run sims once we lock down token size and checkpoint frequency.
maria: Action items:
- maria: write follow-up RFC w/ diagrams, state model, and API examples
- aj: perf sims + latency targets
- devon: durable checkpoint schema + eviction semantics
- andre: billing attribution proposal + security constraints
Sync next Tue 10:30am. :thumbsup:
